The data catalog names each data file (`inputs.raw.visits`), records how to read it, and
keeps a SHA-256 hash of it in `framework.db`. Reads by name are checked against that
hash. This notebook builds the catalog the later notebooks use.

```{python}
#| label: setup
import shutil
import warnings

import framework as fw

root = fw.scaffold()
```

## Bring in the raw files

The study's CSV exports live outside the project in `shared/csv/`. A catalog entry for a
file outside the project would store an absolute path, so the files are copied into
`inputs/raw/` first. Raw files are treated as read-only from here on.

```{python}
shared_csv = root.parent.parent / "shared" / "csv"
raw = root / fw.settings("inputs_raw")

for name in ("participants", "visits", "labs", "survey", "sites"):
    shutil.copy(shared_csv / f"{name}.csv", raw / f"{name}.csv")

sorted(p.name for p in raw.iterdir())
```

## Add files to the catalog

`data_add()` registers a file, records its hash, and writes the entry to
`settings/data.yml`. The name comes from the folder: a file in `inputs/raw` becomes
`inputs.raw.<file>`. Look at the returned entry: the path is relative to the root.

```{python}
fw.data_add(raw / "participants.csv")
```

Files are locked by default, so a changed file stops the next read. The survey export
gets refreshed, so it is added unlocked and only warns on change.

```{python}
fw.data_add(raw / "visits.csv")
fw.data_add(raw / "labs.csv")
fw.data_add(raw / "sites.csv")
fw.data_add(raw / "survey.csv", locked=False)
```

## List and inspect

`data_list()` shows every entry. Check the `locked` column for the survey file.

```{python}
fw.data_list()
```

`data_info()` says how a name will be read: the absolute path, type, delimiter, and lock.

```{python}
fw.data_info("inputs.raw.visits")
```

`columns=True` reads the file and summarizes its layout without showing any values:
each column's type and missing count, and the number of rows. This is how to learn a
restricted file's shape without seeing its records.

```{python}
layout = fw.data_info("inputs.raw.visits", columns=True)
print(layout.rows, "rows")
layout.columns
```

The entries live in `settings/data.yml`, which git tracks, so the catalog travels with
the project.

```{python}
print((root / "settings" / "data.yml").read_text())
```

## Read by name

`data_read()` returns a pandas DataFrame and checks the file's hash first. Missing
blood pressure readings come through as `NaN`.

```{python}
visits = fw.data_read("inputs.raw.visits")
visits.head()
```

```{python}
visits[["systolic_bp", "diastolic_bp", "weight_kg"]].isna().sum()
```

`data_read()` reads CSV with R's readr rules and argument names: only empty cells and
`NA` are missing, whitespace is trimmed, and `na`, `col_types`, `skip`, and `n_max`
work as in R. Here the survey is read with `"very low"` also counted as missing, the
satisfaction column as a factor, and only the first 100 rows.

```{python}
survey = fw.data_read("inputs.raw.survey", na=["", "NA", "very low"],
                      col_types={"satisfaction": "f"}, n_max=100)
print(survey.shape)
survey["satisfaction"].value_counts(dropna=False)
```

A path with a slash reads a file directly, without the catalog or the hash check. A
relative path starts at the project root, so this works from `notebooks/` too.

```{python}
fw.data_read("inputs/raw/sites.csv")
```

## Clean and save

A typical first step: join visits to participants, drop visits without a blood pressure
reading, and keep the analysis columns.

```{python}
participants = fw.data_read("inputs.raw.participants")

bp = (
    visits.merge(participants, on="participant_id")
    .dropna(subset=["systolic_bp", "diastolic_bp"])
    [["participant_id", "site_id", "treatment", "sex", "age", "bmi", "smoker",
      "visit_number", "visit_date", "systolic_bp", "diastolic_bp", "weight_kg"]]
)
bp.shape
```

`data_save()` takes a catalog name, picks the folder from it (`inputs.intermediate.*`
goes to `inputs/intermediate/`), writes Parquet by default, and catalogs the result.
It returns the data so it can end a pipeline; the `;` hides that here.

```{python}
fw.data_save(bp, "inputs.intermediate.bp_visits");
```

An extension on the name picks the format: `inputs.final.bp_analysis.csv` is the catalog
name `inputs.final.bp_analysis`, written as CSV. (`type="csv"` does the same.) This is
the analysis-ready file for later notebooks. CSVs are written as R's
`readr::write_csv()` writes them, so the same data gives the same bytes in both
languages.

```{python}
final = bp.assign(visit_date=lambda d: d["visit_date"].astype(str))
fw.data_save(final, "inputs.final.bp_analysis.csv")
fw.data_list()
```

## Save a database extract

Data can come from a database too. Here the `participant_summary` view from the shared
`study` database is saved and cataloged, so later reads are hash-checked like any file.

```{python}
summary = fw.db_query("SELECT * FROM participant_summary", "study")
fw.data_save(summary, "inputs.intermediate.participant_summary")
fw.data_read("inputs.intermediate.participant_summary").head()
```

## Verify integrity

`data_verify()` compares a file with its recorded hash (and the cloud ledger when the
project has a token; this one doesn't). Look for `[ok]`.

```{python}
fw.data_verify("inputs.raw.participants")
```

Now a deliberate change. A locked file that changes raises `IntegrityError` on the next
read. The demo uses its own small file, so the real inputs stay intact.

```{python}
demo = participants.head(5)
fw.data_save(demo, "inputs.intermediate.integrity_demo", type="csv")

path = fw.data_info("inputs.intermediate.integrity_demo").path
with open(path, "a") as f:
    f.write("999,1,2024-01-01,50,male,25.0,0,control\n")

try:
    fw.data_read("inputs.intermediate.integrity_demo")
except fw.IntegrityError as error:
    print(type(error).__name__, error, sep=": ")
```

`data_verify()` reports the same mismatch, as a warning and `False`.

```{python}
fw.data_verify("inputs.intermediate.integrity_demo")
```

An unlocked file only warns with `DataChangedWarning` and reads the new contents.

```{python}
fw.data_save(demo, "inputs.intermediate.integrity_demo", type="csv", locked=False)
with open(path, "a") as f:
    f.write("998,2,2024-01-02,61,female,31.0,1,intervention\n")

with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
    warnings.simplefilter("always")
    rows = len(fw.data_read("inputs.intermediate.integrity_demo"))
print(rows, "rows;", [w.category.__name__ for w in caught])
```

Saving through `data_save()` again records the new hash, which is how an intended
change is accepted. There is no function to drop a catalog entry, so the demo file stays.

```{python}
fw.data_save(demo, "inputs.intermediate.integrity_demo", type="csv")
fw.data_verify("inputs.intermediate.integrity_demo")
```

## Errors you will meet

A misspelled name raises `DataNotFoundError`.

```{python}
try:
    fw.data_read("inputs.raw.vists")
except fw.DataNotFoundError as error:
    print(error)
```
